title: Highest temperature in Seoul (Incheon) on September 5?

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated KMA and airport briefings through the afternoon will refine resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from global and regional models indicate persistent cloud cover, light rain, and northeasterly flow will cap daytime heating in Tokyo on September 5, positioning 24°C as the most likely daily maximum. These conditions suppress insolation and advect cooler maritime air, keeping temperatures below the early-September climatological average of roughly 27–29°C. Ensemble guidance shows limited warming potential through the afternoon, with observed morning readings already near 22–23°C and little recovery expected. Trader consensus, reflected in the 54% implied probability for 24°C and 26.5% for 25°C, aligns with this model consensus while assigning low odds to outliers above 26°C or below 23°C. Updated runs later today could refine the exact peak if skies clear more than anticipated.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lemd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the China Meteorological Administration and international ensembles point to mostly sunny conditions with light east-northeast winds of 3–4 levels over Qingdao on September 5, 2026, favoring strong daytime heating under a stable high-pressure regime. This setup, following similar clear days with highs of 29–31°C, supports daily maxima near 29–31°C at the official NOAA station at Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport. Trader consensus clusters tightly around 30–32°C because minor differences in peak insolation timing, boundary-layer mixing, and coastal humidity near 55–65% can shift the observed high by 1°C. Limited model spread and no frontal activity keep probabilities balanced, with resolution hinging on the single highest hourly reading.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klax

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: A cold front advancing into São Paulo on September 5 has introduced widespread cloud cover, scattered showers, and cooler maritime air, limiting daytime solar heating and capping the maximum temperature. Official forecasts and model guidance converge on a peak near 21–23°C, with hourly observations showing gradual rises to around 22–23°C amid variable precipitation and southeasterly winds that enhance mixing and evaporative cooling. These conditions contrast with the clearer, warmer regime earlier in the week that produced highs above 26°C. Trader-implied odds remain closely split among the leading outcomes because small differences in rain timing, cloud thickness, or boundary-layer moisture can shift the daily peak by 1–2°C, introducing genuine forecast uncertainty typical of transitional frontal passages in early spring.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zuuu

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models and official guidance from Chinese meteorological sources point to a daytime high near 34°C in Chengdu on September 6, supported by partly cloudy skies, light southerly winds, and minimal precipitation that limits cooling. Recent runs show afternoon peaks potentially reaching 35°C in urban areas due to the Sichuan basin's heat retention and subsidence patterns, while some guidance caps the maximum at 32–33°C if cloud cover increases earlier. These factors explain the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 34–36°C, reflecting uncertainty in exact model consensus and local microclimate effects. Updated numerical weather prediction outputs and the final China Meteorological Administration observation on September 7 will determine resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity, including heavy rainfall and widespread cloud cover over Metro Manila, is the main driver keeping September 6 maximum temperatures clustered in the 29–30°C range. Official forecasts from PAGASA and international models indicate partly to mostly cloudy skies with thunderstorms, which reduce solar insolation and limit afternoon heating compared to drier September climatology near 31°C. Recent yellow and orange rainfall warnings underscore ongoing convective suppression of peaks, with model consensus pointing to highs near 28–30°C rather than extremes. Trader positioning at 40.5% for 30°C and 25% for 29°C reflects this wet pattern, though minor shifts in storm timing or breaks in cloud cover could allow brief spikes toward 31°C. Updated PAGASA briefings and model runs tomorrow morning represent the next key data points.

eventMetadata.context_description: A cold front advancing from the south is the dominant driver suppressing maximum temperatures in São Paulo on September 6, with widespread cloud cover, moderate to heavy rain, and southerly winds limiting daytime solar heating and advecting cooler air masses. Official and ensemble model guidance from sources such as INMET-aligned forecasts and ECMWF runs shows daytime highs clustered around 15–17 °C under overcast conditions and 80–100 % precipitation probability, consistent with the market’s tight clustering on 16 °C (34.5 %) and 17 °C (28.0 %). Differentiation among the leading outcomes hinges on small variations in frontal timing, rainfall intensity, and boundary-layer mixing; stronger or earlier southerly flow and thicker stratiform clouds would favor 15 °C or below, while partial clearing or weaker winds could allow brief warming toward 18 °C. Historical September climatology for the region places typical maxima near 22–24 °C, underscoring the anomalous cooling expected tomorrow.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Toronto Pearson Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=cyyz

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This pattern, with dew points in the mid-teens and modest cloud cover, supports the market-implied odds favoring 22–23°C outcomes at over 74% combined probability. Recent model runs show limited warming potential absent a shift in steering winds, while historical extremes above 30°C remain rare under similar early-September setups. Traders will monitor any final Environment Canada or NOAA updates before resolution based on official daily maximum observations.
